Key trees include S. robusta (Sal), Castanopsis indica (Dhale katus), Ulnus nepalensis (utis), Pinus roxburghii (chir pine), Acacia catechu (khayar), Quercus semicarpifolia (oak), Dalbergia latifolia (satisal), etc. c) Temperate Deciduous forest: It is found at altitudes between 2000 to 3000 m, north of the Sub-Tropical Evergreen forest. Trees like Castanopsis indica (kattus), Schima wallichii (chilaune), Macaranga Nepalensis (malato), Pinus spp., Fagus sylvatica (beech), Ulmus americana (elm), Rhododendron arboreum (rhododendron), etc., are present. d) Temperate Coniferous evergreen forest: It exists at altitudes between 3000 to 4000 m in the Mahabharat ranges. This forest type, situated above the temperate forest, includes trees like cones, laliguras, Betula utilis (bhojpatra), pine, Abir spp. (fir), and Quercus leucotrichophora (oak). e) Alpine Vegetation: It grows at altitudes between 4000 to 5000 m in the Himalayan region, where the climate is cold and dry. Trees are absent, and only thorny bushes are found. It includes: Rhododendron lepidotum (sunpaati), Caltha palustris (caltha) f) Tundra vegetation: It is found at altitudes above 5000 m in the higher Himalayan regions covered with snow, forming a cold desert area. This area contains vegetation such as lichens and mosses.
PRESENT STATE OF VEGETATION IN NEPAL
A joint five-year survey conducted by the Department of Forest Research and Survey and the National forest Products Survey Project in between 2067 to 2071 BS, has come up with following findings:

1. Roughly 44% of Nepal's landmass is occupied by forest. 2. Forest roughly occupies 5.96 million hectares of landmass of the country. 3. Protected forests in Nepal make up about 12.1% of the total, and conserved forests

account for around 21.4%. 4. Approximately 5.1% of Nepal's forests are classified as production forests. 5. Between 2000 and 2005, Nepal lost about 2,640 square kilometers (1,019 square miles) of forest, with an annual deforestation rate of about 1.4%, equivalent to an average loss of 530 square kilometers (205 square miles) each year. 6. A 2010 study estimated that 39.1% of Nepal is covered by forests, and agriculture occupies 29.83% of the land. 7. Patch and edge forests, constituting 23.4% of the national forest cover, show interactions with surrounding living things. 8. Core forests make up 79.3% of protected areas and 63% of the area outside protected areas.
